minutes_text:
MINUTES

  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JULY 5, 2018

An adjourned regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by MAYOR HUFF at 4:06 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive
North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz and Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  Zerunyan.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis (via teleconference)
  Planning Director David Wahha
  Traffic Engineering Deputy Joanne Itagaki
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT

NONE.

5.  CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 29-16: CONSTRUCTION HOURS FOR PV PENINSULA
  WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH BETWEEN
  DAPPLEGRAY LANE AND MONTECILLO DRIVE

  Recommendation: That the City Council (1) Continue to take public testimony; (2)
  Discuss the issues; (3) Close the Public Hearing; (4) Approve CWS’ request to shift work
  between Dapplegray Lane to Montecillo Drive from overnight work to daytime work,
  subject to final approval by the City’s Traffic Engineering Deputy.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and reviewed
  the information that has been received since the last meeting, including the third party
  review of the noise analysis which was conducted by the City’s environmental
  consultant, Environmental Science Associates (ESA). He further provided information
  on the updated traffic control plan that will be implemented if the proposed daytime
  work is approved.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JULY 5, 2018
   Carmelo Sorce, Director of Engineering addressed the City Council to express Cal
  Water’s appreciation for the City’s diligence in consideration of this matter and
  introduced the other Cal Water officials present. Mr. Sorce further reviewed Cal Water’s
  request to switch from nighttime construction to daytime construction for a portion of
  the project and introduced Amir Yazdanniyaz, Acoustical Engineering Services (AES)
  who conducted the nose analysis on behalf of Cal Water.

  Mr. Yazdanniyaz reviewed the methodology used to conduct the sound study, reiterating
  the fact the results show that the use of sound walls will have a minimal affect on
  reducing the noise impacts.

  Mr. Sorce reviewed the traffic analysis noting that the additional delay in travel time for
  the two reaches being discussed will be minimal. He further reviewed the additional
  traffic considerations being implemented during the construction.

  Allen Sako, Environmental Science Associates (ESA) reviewed the results of ESA’s third
  party analysis of the noise study and responded to inquiries from the City Council
  regarding the noise study.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, he noted that their results regarding
  nighttime ambient noise levels are similar to the results found by AES.
  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that the threshold of 50 dB during nighttime
  work is a very low threshold. Mr. Sako concurred.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ, Mr. Sako noted that he has reviewed AES’
  responses to the questions posed during the third party review and AES has sufficiently
  answered each of the questions raised.

  Discussion ensued concerning the noise impact of the nighttime work and the noise
  threshold. It was noted that the only way to change the noise threshold would be to
  recirculate the environmental document and amend the Mitigated Negative Declaration.

  Further discussion ensued concerning the traffic study and the expected traffic delays.
  Mr. Sorce commented that the signal light timing will be adjusted based on traffic
  patterns and there will be traffic control officers at certain intersections to immediately
  address traffic issues.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL regarding the noise mitigation measures
  at the lay down site, Mr. Sorce commented that sound walls will be used if necessary.

  Further discussion ensued concerning the project timeline/schedule and road closures
  associated with the different portions of the project. It was noted that this information
  is also posted the Cal Water web site at pvpwaterproject.com.

  MAYOR HUFF called for further public comment. There was no further comment.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JULY 5, 2018
   COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE
  COMPANY’S REQUEST TO SHIFT WORK BETWEEN DAPPLEGRAY LANE TO
  MONTECILLO DRIVE FROM OVERNIGHT WORK TO DAYTIME WORK, SUBJECT
  TO FINAL APPROVAL BY THE CITY’S TRAFFIC ENGINEER.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman

6.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 4:52 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular
  meeting of the City Council scheduled for Monday, July 10, 2018 p.m. in the Council
  Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
  Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JULY 5, 2018
